children: Japanese rubber futures fell on Friday, tracking a plunge in Tokyo equities as investors unwound positions in a global equities rout, putting the contract on track for its biggest weekly loss since the week ended June 26.
The Osaka Exchange (OSE) rubber contract for April delivery
was down 8.4 yen, or 1.94%, at 424.9 yen ($2.69) per kg as of 0150 GMT. It touched its lowest since September 16 earlier in the day
The contract has lost 3.96% so far this week, declining for the fourth consecutive week
The rubber contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) for January delivery
fell 410 yuan, or 2.16%, to 18,530 yuan ($2,778.94) per metric ton
The most active December butadiene rubber contract on the SHFE (SHBRv1) fell 270 yuan, or 1.72%, to 15,385 yuan per metric ton

Japan's Nikkei share average fell more than 5% on Friday as fears of regulatory scrutiny and a slowdown in the AI buildout weighed on sentiment following the Democratic sweep in the US midterm elections, with the Nikkei
down 5.5% 18 minutes into the trading day
Rubber is likely being affected by sentiment in equity markets, with the market unwinding positions and adjusting for risk, a Singapore-based trader said
strengthened 0.2% to a one-week high of 157.40 a US dollar before reversing some of that gain, as a sharp selloff in US equities drove investors toward haven assets
A stronger currency makes yen-denominated assets less affordable to overseas buyers

Thailand's rubber production is forecast to rise 1.5% to about 4.9 million tons in 2026, as high prices stimulate tapping and the risk of leaf-fall disease eases, analysts at rubber information provider Qinrex said in a note
The front-month rubber contract on Singapore Exchange's SICOM platform for January delivery (STFF7) last traded at 236.9 US cents per kg, down 2.3%
